W1-006.claim: The span 2:5-2:13 is a sound unit (rounds two and three of the exchange and their outcome, the death decree), but its onset edge is the same 2:4/2:5 edge that the row before it grades medium_low and calls weak. This row grades medium and does not weigh that edge at all. One edge cannot carry two grades.

suggested_fix.fact: The onset of this row at 2:5 rests on a dialogue turn alone: the king's speech answers the reply of 2:4 and opens with a weak answering formula, and no mark follows 2:4. The grade should say so, as the grade of the row before it does.

W1-006.claim: The row lists the answering formula at 2:5, 2:7, 2:8 and 2:10 under one unqualified name, but at 2:10 the formula is held only by the inventory's loose class; the strict class holds 2:5, 2:7 and 2:8 in this span. The neighbouring row marks its own loose-only verse (2:15) as loose, so 2:10 here reads as a strict hit, which the layer does not hold.

suggested_fix.fact: at 2:10 the answering formula belongs to the loose class only (the two verbs are words 1 and 5 of the verse); 2:5, 2:7 and 2:8 are in the strict class

W1-007.claim: The cut at 2:16/2:17 is right, but the rationale gives the paragraph mark as the reason the movement ends ('ends at the PE after 2:16'). A mark informs and does not decide. The text grounds exist and sit only in the rejected-alternative field: 2:16 ends Daniel's steps at court with his request to the king, and 2:17 moves him to his house and to new hearers.

suggested_fix.fact: The close of this row rests on the text: the audience with the king at 2:16 ends the court steps, and 2:17 changes place and hearers. The PE after 2:16 is single-witness information beside that, not the ground.

W1-008.claim: The span 2:17-2:19 is one narrative movement and its onset at 2:16/2:17 is sound, but its close at 2:19/2:20 is argued from the onset side only. The last clause of 2:19 states that Daniel blessed the God of heaven, and the praise of 2:20-2:23 is that blessing spoken; the device inventory holds the blessing word on both sides of the seam (2:19 and 2:20), and the opening of 2:20 is the answered-and-said connective, which the book's rules treat as too weak to open a unit alone. The row grades itself medium while the row across the same seam is medium_low.

suggested_fix.fact: The close seam is weighed from both sides: the blessing announced in the last clause of 2:19 is delivered in 2:20-2:23, the blessing word stands on each side of the seam, and the speaker formula of 2:20 is a weak connective; the seam rests on the change of form alone, and the grade follows that.

W1-008.claim: The boundary 2:17-2:19 holds on the Masoretic bytes; the one defect is in the device note, where MEASURED is set beside a layer with no script named and the same tier is left to cover the genre word 'narrative'.

suggested_fix.fact: The language of 2:17-2:19 is Aramaic as read from the language-zone file (the tier that matches a pinned file read); the genre label is a reading and carries its own tier.

W1-009.claim: The praise 2:20-2:23 is truly described and its marks and ketiv/qere site are truly reported; the defect is the device note's tier, MEASURED beside a layer with no script, covering the genre word 'hymn' as well as the language.

suggested_fix.fact: The language of 2:20-2:23 is Aramaic as read from the language-zone file; that the passage is a hymn is the row's reading with its own tier.

W1-010.claim: The unit 2:24-2:30 and its medium_low grade are sound: Daniel's approach through Arioch, the king's question and Daniel's preamble run to 2:30, and the dream report opens at 2:31. The defect is a disclosure gap: the mark layer holds an OSHB editorial note at 2:29 (an anomalous form, and a ketiv/qere kept or dropped against BHS) that the row does not disclose, although the same writer part discloses the same kind of note at 2:37, 2:38, 2:39 and 2:41.

suggested_fix.fact: An OSHB editorial note stands at 2:29 (single witness); it is disclosed and no seam is argued from it.

W1-010.claim: 2:29 carries two OSHB editorial notes (an anomalous form, and a ketiv/qere added or abandoned relative to BHS) that the row does not disclose, while the sibling row for 2:36-2:45 discloses the same class of note; the boundary itself and both interior marks are truly reported.

suggested_fix.fact: Editorial notes of the single witness stand at 2:29 (anomalous form; ketiv/qere handling differs from BHS) and are disclosed as such; the answered-and-said formula at 2:27 is the loose form (three words between the verbs), the strict form standing only at 2:26.

W1-011.claim: 2:31-2:35 is a coherent dream report: it opens with the seeing formula and behold at 2:31, steps once at 2:34 with the seeing-until formula, and ends with the stone filling the earth at 2:35; 2:36 then names the dream as told and announces its reading. The unit, type and grade stand. The defect is a disclosure gap: the mark layer holds an OSHB editorial note at 2:31 that the row does not disclose.

suggested_fix.fact: An OSHB editorial note stands at 2:31 (single witness); it is disclosed and no seam is argued from it.

W1-011.claim: 2:31, the verse the row's own Aramaic quotation is taken from, carries two OSHB editorial notes (anomalous form; ketiv/qere handling differs from BHS) that the row does not disclose; the quotation itself is exact and does not include the word those notes most plausibly concern.

suggested_fix.fact: Editorial notes of the single witness stand at 2:31 (anomalous form; ketiv/qere handling differs from BHS) beside the two ketiv/qere sites of 2:33.

W1-012.claim: 2:36-2:45 is one interpretation and should stay one row, but the ground the row gives for rejecting a cut at 2:43/2:44 is not the ground that holds. The rule it cites concerns where a report parts from its interpretation (2:35/2:36); it says nothing about a cut inside the interpretation. What holds is in the text: 2:44 opens with a time phrase that depends on the kings of 2:37-2:43, and 2:45 returns to the stone of 2:34 and ends on the certainty formula, so 2:44-2:45 cannot stand apart. The row also exceeds nine verses and says it is a single speech act, but it does not say that no internal signal divides it, which is the condition for the exception; and its speech-act claim is loose, since Daniel's speech runs from 2:27 and is already divided at 2:30/2:31 and 2:35/2:36.

suggested_fix.fact: A cut at 2:43/2:44 is declined on the text: the time phrase that opens 2:44 refers to the kings of the verses before it, and 2:45 reads the stone of the report and closes on the certainty of dream and interpretation. The row states that no internal signal of a new unit stands inside 2:36-2:45, the time phrase at 2:44 being a link back.

W1-012.claim: The gloss attached to the Aramaic quotation of 2:36 runs five consecutive WEB words of web:Dan.2.36 (“This is the dream; and”) without curly quotes or a web reference in that field; every Masoretic fact the row asserts, including its complete ketiv/qere list and its editorial-note list, is true on the mark layer.

suggested_fix.fact: The gloss of the 2:36 quotation is the row's own rendering of the four Aramaic words and does not reproduce the WEB wording across its semicolon; or it is marked as a WEB quotation with its reference.

W1-013.claim: 2:46-2:49 is a sound closing narrative: the king's prostration, his confession, Daniel's promotion and the appointment of the three at Daniel's request, ending with Daniel at the king's gate. Keeping 2:49 inside the row is right, because 2:49 depends on the promotion of 2:48 and has no reach beyond the scene. The defect is in the wording of the ground: boundary_rationale says the chapter ends at 2:49. A chapter line may neither drive nor corroborate a seam, and the row has the text's own grounds to hand: the appointment notice of 2:49 and the subject-first royal clause of 3:1.

suggested_fix.fact: The unit closes on the appointment of the three and Daniel's station at the king's gate at 2:49, and the next verse opens with a subject-first royal clause and a new action; the close is stated without reference to the chapter.

W1-013.claim: The closing scene 2:46-2:49 is bounded by a PE on each side and every formula and quotation it cites is on the bytes; the one defect is the device note's tier, MEASURED beside a layer with no script, covering the genre phrase 'narrative close' as well as the language.

suggested_fix.fact: The language of 2:46-2:49 is Aramaic as read from the language-zone file; that the verses are a narrative close is the row's reading with its own tier.

W2-001.claim: 3:1-3:7 is one movement (image set up 3:1, officials gathered 3:2-3:3, the herald's command 3:4-3:6, compliance 3:7) and both edges are sound. The defect is narrow: the rejected-alternative field holds a verse count (3:1-3:3 as a three-verse setting) and two readings (the command of 3:4-3:6 is embedded in narration; 3:7 is its fulfilment) with no tier word.

suggested_fix.fact: the size of the setting is a span count and the embedding of the herald's command with its fulfilment is a reading; each owes its own tier

W2-001.claim: The row says the music list of 3:5 recurs in the execution clause of 3:7. That is exact on the WEB, which the warrant cites, but not on the Masoretic bytes: in WLC the list at 3:5 runs nine words from the horn to the summary phrase and the list at 3:7 runs eight, the sixth instrument of 3:5 being absent at 3:7 (it stands again at 3:10 and 3:15). The recurrence still binds command to compliance; the row states it more fully than the Aramaic holds.

suggested_fix.fact: In the WLC text the instrument list of the execution clause is one instrument shorter than the list in the herald's order; the recurrence is complete only in the WEB rendering

W2-002.claim: 3:8-3:12 is a coherent accusation unit and both edges are sound, but the ground given for unit_type dialogue does not match the text: the king's speech at 3:14 is addressed to the three accused, not to the accusers, and the accusers get no spoken reply (3:13 is a summons). The row holds one narrated verse (3:8) and one party's speech (3:9-3:12), so no exchange of speeches lies inside it.

suggested_fix.fact: the king's words at 3:14 are spoken to the three accused men; the accusers are answered by an act, the summons of 3:13, so the row is a one-party address and its type has to be argued on that footing

W2-002.claim: Every Aramaic and mark fact in the row is true on the bytes, but the boundary_rationale and the strongest_rejected_alternative carry no tier word: the SAMEKH after 3:12 is a witness fact stated twice without its tier or the layer that holds it, and the rejected alternative holds two counts (11 verses for 3:8-18; the nine-verse limit) without a tier.

suggested_fix.fact: The SAMEKH after 3:12 is an extracted single-witness fact of the WLC mark layer, and the verse counts in the rejected alternative are measured counts

W2-003.claim: 3:13-3:18 is one exchange (summons 3:13, the king's question 3:14-3:15, the three's answer 3:16-3:18) and both edges are sound. The defect: boundary_rationale carries no tier word although it holds two mark claims (SAMEKH after 3:12 and after 3:18), one device claim (the weak opener of 3:13) and the reading that the speaker change carries the onset.

suggested_fix.fact: the two SAMEKH marks are facts of the single-witness mark layer and the weak opener is a fact of the device inventory; the weight given to the speaker change is a reading

W2-003.claim: The two SAMEKH marks that bracket the exchange (after 3:12 and after 3:18) are true in the mark layer, but the boundary_rationale states both without any tier word or named layer; the field has no tier word at all.

suggested_fix.fact: The SAMEKH after 3:12 and the SAMEKH after 3:18 are extracted single-witness facts of the WLC mark layer

W2-004.claim: 3:19-3:23 (fury, orders, binding, the executioners' death, the fall into the furnace) is a defensible unit and medium_low is the honest grade for the 3:23/3:24 edge. The defect: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative carry no tier word although they hold mark claims (SAMEKH after 3:18, PE after 3:23), a device claim (the weak opener at 3:19 and 3:24) and the count of 9 verses for 3:19-3:27.

suggested_fix.fact: the PE after 3:23 and the SAMEKH after 3:18 are single-witness mark-layer facts, the weak openers are device-inventory facts, 3:19-3:27 is nine verses by count, and the shift from the executors to the king is a reading

W2-004.claim: The mark facts are true (SAMEKH after 3:18, PE after 3:23) and the close is honestly graded, but neither the boundary_rationale nor the strongest_rejected_alternative carries a tier word: the two marks and the count of nine verses for 3:19-27 stand untiered. The device_notes also state where the Greek tradition places its additional prayer and hymn with no tier; no pinned layer holds that fact, so its true tier is a report.

suggested_fix.fact: The SAMEKH after 3:18 and the PE after 3:23 are extracted single-witness facts of the WLC mark layer; 3:19-27 is a measured nine verses; the Greek placement is a reported fact

W2-005.claim: 3:24-3:27 (the king's astonishment, the four in the fire, the call to come out, the officials' inspection) is one movement of discovery and public witness, and its edges are honestly graded. The defect: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative carry no tier word although they hold mark claims (PE after 3:23, SAMEKH after 3:25), device claims (the blessing formula at 3:28; the weak opener at 3:26) and a count (two rows of two verses).

suggested_fix.fact: the PE after 3:23 and the SAMEKH after 3:25 are single-witness mark-layer facts, the blessing formula at 3:28 and the weak opener of 3:26 are device-inventory facts, 3:24-3:25 and 3:26-3:27 are two verses each by count, and the dependence of the call on the sight is a reading

W2-005.claim: The mark facts are true (PE after 3:23, SAMEKH after 3:25) and the inner SAMEKH is disclosed and weighed, but the boundary_rationale and the strongest_rejected_alternative carry no tier word for them. One extent point in device_notes: the WEB words quoted for the two-word Aramaic splice at 3:25 begin with 'like', which renders the participle standing before the splice, so the WEB quotation reaches one Aramaic word further back than the splice.

suggested_fix.fact: The PE after 3:23 and the SAMEKH after 3:25 are extracted single-witness facts of the WLC mark layer; the WEB phrase for the fourth figure renders the participle together with the two-word phrase

W2-006.claim: 3:28-3:29 is one royal speech (blessing 3:28, decree with its ground 3:29) and both edges are sound. The defect: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative carry no tier word although they hold two device claims (the blessing formula at 3:28, the decree formula at 3:29), a mark claim (PE after 3:30) and the reading that 3:30 lies outside the quoted speech.

suggested_fix.fact: the blessing formula at 3:28 and the decree formula at 3:29 are device-inventory facts, the PE after 3:30 is a single-witness mark-layer fact, and the end of the quoted speech at 3:29 is read from the text

W2-006.claim: The Aramaic facts are true: 3:28 opens with the answer formula and the blessing word, 3:29 carries the decree formula, and a PE follows 3:30. The boundary_rationale and the strongest_rejected_alternative carry no tier word, so the PE and the two formula occurrences stand untiered, as does the reading that 3:30 lies outside the quoted speech.

suggested_fix.fact: The PE after 3:30 is an extracted single-witness fact of the WLC mark layer; the blessing word at 3:28 and the decree formula at 3:29 are extracted device occurrences

W2-008.claim: web:Dan.4.1-4.3 = oshb:Dan.3.31-3.33 is a coherent prescript (sender, addressees, greeting; statement of purpose; doxology) and both edges sit where the form puts them. Two defects. First, boundary_rationale names the addressees in a run of five consecutive words of the World English Bible at web:Dan.4.1 = oshb:Dan.3.31 without quotation marks. Second, the backward rival is declined only because a row may not cross the parent seam, and the middle verse, which states the letter's purpose and points forward, is never used.

suggested_fix.fact: the addressees are named either in the row's own words or as a marked quotation with its reference; and the middle verse announces what the Most High God did to the king himself, which is the subject of the account that follows and not of the furnace account before

W2-008.claim: In boundary_rationale the addressee phrase 'the peoples, nations and languages' is five consecutive WEB words of web:Dan.4.1 (MT 3:31) standing outside curly quotes. Every Aramaic, mark and numbering fact in the row is otherwise true, and every reference in the zone is written dual.

suggested_fix.fact: The addressee phrase is either quoted from the verse with its reference or stated in other words

W3-001.claim: 5:1-5:4 is one movement (feast, vessels, praise of the idols) and both its edges fall where the form says; but the row lists the chapter line among its onset signals, and it calls the unit before the seam a decree although the verse before the seam (web:Dan.4.37 = oshb:Dan.4.34) is first-person praise.

suggested_fix.fact: the onset signal at 5:1 is the subject-first royal clause that names the new king before the verb; a chapter line is not a signal and is removed from the signal list; the verse before the seam is first-person praise, not a decree

W3-003.claim: 5:10-5:12 is a coherent unit, the queen's speech from her entry to her closing request; but in device_notes the word EXTRACTED is set beside a reading (that the phrase at 5:11 recalls the earlier reign as Daniel's credential), and the inventory holds only the presence of the phrase at 5:11.

suggested_fix.fact: the inventory holds the presence of in_the_days_of_aram at 5:11 (that part is EXTRACTED); that the phrase serves as Daniel's credential is a reading and takes INFERRED

W3-003.claim: In device_notes the word EXTRACTED, naming the device inventory, stands on a sentence whose second half is a reading: the inventory holds the in-the-days-of phrase at oshb:Dan.5.11, and nothing in that layer holds that the phrase serves as Daniel's credential. Every mark, count and quotation fact of the row is true.

suggested_fix.fact: the phrase is a listed formula at this verse (EXTRACTED); that it recalls the earlier reign as the ground of Daniel's standing is a reading (INFERRED)

W3-004.claim: 5:13-5:16 is a coherent unit, the king's address to Daniel ending on the offer, and both edges are sound; but the rival the row weighs (an onset at 5:14) is not the strongest one. The stronger rival puts the close one verse later, after 5:17, so that the king's offer and Daniel's answer to it stand together and the recital opens at 5:18.

suggested_fix.fact: the strongest rival is a close after 5:17, joining Daniel's refusal of the gifts to the offer it answers and opening the recital at the direct address of 5:18; it is declined because the speaker changes at 5:17 with a full speech frame and a PE (one witness) follows 5:16, while 5:17/5:18 has neither

W3-007.claim: 5:29-5:30 is a sound closing unit (the promised reward given, then the king's death in that night) and its close is the parent seam, two-sided; but strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes carry claims with no tier word.

suggested_fix.fact: that the reward completes the arc the death notice seals is a reading and takes INFERRED; the K/Q presence at 5:29 and 5:30 is held by the K/Q layer of the single witness and takes EXTRACTED with that layer named

W3-007.claim: Two fields carry claims with no tier word. device_notes states that the verse of the quotation is a ketiv/qere verse and that the sites at 5:29 and 5:30 are disclosed, which is in effect the list of such sites in the span; the mark layer holds exactly one at each verse and no other, so the list is true and can be tiered against that layer. strongest_rejected_alternative states that the reward completes the arc the death notice seals, a reading, with no tier. Every mark, formula and quotation fact of the row is true.

suggested_fix.fact: the span has two ketiv/qere sites, one in each verse, and no other (a count over the mark layer, MEASURED); the weighing of reward and death notice as one arc is a reading (INFERRED)

W3-008.claim: The row's rejected rival (the succession verse web:Dan.5.31 = oshb:Dan.6.1 standing alone as a notice) is turned down partly because no mark follows that verse. The silence is real, but a missing mark is not evidence against a rival; only the dependence of the appointments on the succession verse is a text reason. The span itself is a coherent setting unit and its boundaries stand.

suggested_fix.fact: The one-verse rival is rejected on the text alone: the appointments that follow depend on the succession verse for their king. The absence of a mark after that verse is a single-witness silence to disclose, not a reason.

W3-008.claim: The boundary_rationale states the petuchah after 5:30 as 'single-witness' with no tier word and no layer named; the fact itself is true (mark layer: PE recorded on MT 5:30). Everything else the row asserts about the Masoretic layer collates: the Aramaic splice is an exact substring at the head of oshb:Dan.6.1 (= web:Dan.5.31), no paragraph mark follows MT 6:1, 6:2, 6:3 or 6:4, and the span holds no paseq and no ketiv/qere entry.

suggested_fix.fact: the petuchah after MT 5:30 is a fact extracted from the single-witness WLC mark layer; give it that tier and name that layer in the rationale, as the row's other fields already do for the absence of a mark

W3-009.claim: The boundary_rationale rests both seams on formula facts (the then-connective at web:Dan.6.4 = oshb:Dan.6.5 and the because-of-this connective at web:Dan.6.9 = oshb:Dan.6.10) without a tier word or a named layer; both facts are true in the device inventory and on the bytes. The row's mark claims are true in both directions: setumah after MT 6:6 only, one paseq at MT 6:8, no ketiv/qere in MT 6:5-6:10.

suggested_fix.fact: the two connectives at the seams are formula hits extracted from the device inventory; give them that tier and layer where the rationale leans on them

W3-011.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative gives a count ('nine verses') with no tier; the count is true (web:Dan.6.16-6.24 = oshb:Dan.6.17-6.25). The row's Masoretic claims all hold: no mark on either seam, one ketiv/qere verse in the span (MT 6:17), disclosed and outside the quoted splice, and no paseq.

suggested_fix.fact: the rival unit runs nine verses, a count that can be measured on the verse list; give it its tier

W3-012.claim: The boundary_rationale leans on the then-connective at web:Dan.6.19 = oshb:Dan.6.20 without a tier or a layer; the fact is true (inventory hit and bytes). All other original-language claims hold: the splice is exact, the two ketiv/qere verses of the span (MT 6:21 and MT 6:23) are both disclosed and no other exists, and the span has no mark and no paseq.

suggested_fix.fact: the connective at the onset is a formula hit extracted from the device inventory; give it that tier and layer

W3-013.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative states a reading about voice (the notice is the narrator's, not the king's) and a rule about closing notices with no tier, and device_notes gives the paseq count with no tier. The facts are sound: MT 6:27 has two paseq, MT 6:26 and 6:27 each have one ketiv/qere entry and MT 6:28 has none, and the four formulae sit where the row puts them.

suggested_fix.fact: the change of voice between the letter and the notice is a reading of the text and should be tiered as one; the paseq count is extracted from the single-witness mark layer

W4-001.claim: The span 7:1-7:6 is a sound unit and its medium_low grade is honest, but one reference line places the weak connective of 7:1 at word 12, while the witness line for oshb:Dan.7.1 has בֵּאדַ֨יִן֙ as its token 13 of 18; the word-position convention of the language-zone layer is the split-token one (it ends the Aramaic run at Dan.7.28 w16, and the witness line for 7:28 has 16 tokens). suggested_fix.fact: the weak connective of 7:1 is the thirteenth token of the verse in the witness extract (or the position is dropped, since no layer records it)

W4-001.claim: The onset reference places the Aramaic 'then' of 7:1 at word 12, but on the witness bytes it is word 13 of the verse's 18 space-delimited words, the count the language-zone layer also uses (it ends the Aramaic run at 7:28 word 16, and 7:28 has 16 such words). Every other Aramaic fact of the row holds.

suggested_fix.fact: the 'then' word of 7:1 is word 13 of 18 on the one-based count shared with the language-zone layer; or drop the position and keep the verse

W4-002.claim: All Aramaic splices, the mark disclosures and the language claim of the row hold on the bytes; the one defect is that the rejected-alternative field states, with no tier word, that 7:11 resumes the horn of 7:8.

suggested_fix.fact: the link of 7:11 to 7:8 is a reading from shared wording (the speaking stem and the great-things adjective stand in both verses) and carries the tier of a reading

W4-003.claim: The row says 7:14 ends on the everlasting-dominion clause and quotes three words; on the bytes those are words 12-14 of 21 and 7 words follow. The rationale field also carries no tier word for its device and mark facts. The splices themselves are exact.

suggested_fix.fact: the quoted three words begin the closing sentence of 7:14; the verse's last words are the kingdom-not-destroyed clause. Each device hit and the petuchah carry the tier of the layer holding them

W4-004.claim: The Aramaic splices and the measured stem counts of the row reproduce exactly; the defect is that the rejected-alternative field has no tier word for its byte claim that the reply frame at the end of 7:16 opens the answer, nor for its over-split judgment.

suggested_fix.fact: the last five words of 7:16 are the reply frame (he said to me, and made the interpretation known); that is a fact of the witness bytes, and the over-split judgment is a reading

W4-007.claim: Every Aramaic and Hebrew fact of the one-verse notice holds, including the language return at 8:1 word 1 and the petuchah after 7:28; the one defect is that the rejected-alternative field states, with no tier word, that 7:28 changes speaker back to the seer.

suggested_fix.fact: the speaker change at 7:28 is a reading of the first-person Daniel formula there (a device-inventory hit at 7:28) and carries its tier

W4-009.claim: The interior note '8:6 has i_saw_heb' is true of the inventory layer but the form at 8:6 stands in a relative clause that looks back to the ram already seen at 8:3; the fresh first-person seeing verb of the span stands at the head of 8:7 and is not mentioned. W5-001.claim: The span 9:1-9:3 is a sound unit and both edges stand, but two readings carry a witness tier. The rationale says the repeated year formula of 9:2 is texture and opens nothing under an EXTRACTED tag, while the device notes give the same reading as INFERRED; the witness holds the formula, and the device inventory holds it as a dateline entry at 9:2, but neither holds its status as texture. W5-001.claim: In boundary_rationale the sentence on 9:2 carries the tier EXTRACTED OSHB/WLC for the statement that the repeated year formula is texture and opens nothing. The witness holds the formula at 9:2 words 1-3 and the device inventory lists 9:2 among its eight dateline entries; that it opens no unit is a reading, and the same row's device_notes tiers that reading INFERRED. The stronger word stands on the weaker fact.

suggested_fix.fact: The presence of the year formula at 9:2 is in the witness and in the dateline inventory; that it resumes 9:1 and opens no unit is a reading and takes the weaker tier, as device_notes already has it.

W5-003.claim: Two WEB quotations set beside a Hebrew splice as its rendering cover more than the splice. At 9:17 the splice is words 1-2 while the quotation renders words 1-6, and the English places the vocative before the verb where the Hebrew has it after. At 9:20 the splice is words 1-3 while the quotation renders words 1-5. The 9:15 and 9:19 pairs are co-extensive. Every Hebrew and mark fact in the row is otherwise true on the bytes.

suggested_fix.fact: Either the Hebrew cited at 9:17 and 9:20 runs as far as the English quoted beside it, or the English is said to render the whole clause and not only the cited words.

W5-004.claim: The span 9:20-9:23 and its type are defensible, but two statements about the speech verb of 9:22 put a decision under a witness tier: the rationale says the verb of saying is a weak connective and is not used as an onset, under EXTRACTED tags, and the device notes say it opens no unit, under an EXTRACTED tag. The witness and the inventory hold the verb at 9:22; that it opens no unit is the row's decision.

suggested_fix.fact: The verb of saying stands in 9:22 after the two narrated verbs, so the messenger's speech begins inside the verse; that it does not open a unit is a reading (INFERRED). It follows that no verse-level cut separates the narration from the speech, which bears on the 9:21/9:22 rival.

W5-004.claim: The 9:22 splice and the WEB quotation set beside it do not cover the same words, and the splice is described as opening the messenger's words though it starts one word earlier. The splice is words 3-6 of 9:22; word 3 carries the atnah and closes the narrated clause, the verb of saying is word 4, and the speech proper begins at word 5. The WEB quotation renders words 1-4. So the English covers two words the Hebrew does not show, and the Hebrew shows two words the English does not render.

suggested_fix.fact: At 9:22 the narrated clause ends at word 3 under the atnah, the verb of saying is word 4 and the address to Daniel begins at word 5; the Hebrew cited and the English quoted should cover the same words.

W5-005.claim: Two WEB quotations set beside a Hebrew splice run past it. At 9:24 the splice is words 1-2 and the quotation also renders word 3, the verb. At 10:1 the splice is words 1-3 and the quotation also renders words 4-5, the royal title. Every Hebrew, mark, K/Q and paseq fact in the row is otherwise true on the bytes, and the Masoretic layer supports the close where the row puts it.

suggested_fix.fact: Either the Hebrew cited at 9:24 and 10:1 runs as far as the English quoted beside it (through the verb at 9:24 word 3 and the title at 10:1 words 4-5), or the English is said to render more than the cited words.

W6-002.claim: The unit and both its edges are right as form: 10:4-10:9 is the sighting, opened by the date-and-place clause that the lifted-eyes formula of 10:5 completes and closed by the seer's collapse at 10:9. One defect of quotation hygiene: the evidence-refs entry for 10:7 runs five consecutive words of web:Dan.10.7 (“I, Daniel, alone saw the”) without quotation marks and without a web reference.

suggested_fix.fact: the 10:7 disclosure either describes the Hebrew in words that do not follow the translation for five words running, or carries the translation's words as a marked quotation with its web reference

W6-002.claim: One evidence label for 10:7 carries five consecutive WEB words of that verse (the run 'I Daniel alone saw the', punctuation aside) with no curly quotes and no web reference in that field; every Hebrew and mark fact of the row is otherwise true on the bytes.

suggested_fix.fact: the label for 10:7 either paraphrases in fewer than five consecutive WEB words or carries the quotation convention with its web reference

W6-003.claim: The unit is right as form: the touch at 10:10 raises the seer, the address formula at 10:11 opens the messenger's first speech, the speech ends at 10:14, and 10:15 looks back on it. Medium is earned, since both edges are two-sided. One defect of quotation hygiene: the evidence-refs entry for 10:10 is word for word the first five words of web:Dan.10.10 (“Behold, a hand touched me”) with no quotation marks and no web reference.

suggested_fix.fact: the 10:10 onset entry either describes the touch in words of its own or carries the translation's five words as a marked quotation with its web reference

W6-003.claim: The row lists a year word at 10:13, but 10:13 holds no year word: the match is a consonant string inside the adjective הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים (the chief princes), which the device layer itself classes as a substring artifact and drops from its word-anchored list; the time word 10:13 does hold is the day word י֔וֹם.

suggested_fix.fact: 10:13 carries a day word (twenty-one days) and no year word; the year-word signal there is a substring artifact

W6-005.claim: The unit is right as form and its grade is honest: 10:20-11:1 is the messenger's preamble, and 11:1 belongs with it because it continues the first-person account of standing with Michael that ends 10:21, while 11:2 takes up the promise of 10:21 and begins the survey. The rival at 10:21/11:1, with its PE, is the strongest one and is named. One minor defect: the evidence-refs entry for 10:20 follows web:Dan.10.20 for five consecutive words (“he said, “Do you know” in the translation's order) without quotation marks or a web reference. This is the weakest finding of the cluster: the run crosses the opening of the quoted speech.

suggested_fix.fact: the 10:20 onset entry describes the messenger's question in words that do not track the translation for five words running, or quotes it with marks and its web reference

W6-005.claim: One evidence label for 10:20 carries five consecutive WEB words of that verse (the run 'he said do you know', punctuation aside) with no curly quotes and no web reference in that field; every Hebrew, mark and dateline fact of the row is otherwise true on the bytes.

suggested_fix.fact: the label for 10:20 either paraphrases in fewer than five consecutive WEB words or carries the quotation convention with its web reference

W6-006.claim: The unit stands as form: the survey opens at 11:2 and the first text signal after it is the succession wording at 11:7. But the onset sentence of boundary_rationale sets the Hebrew opening clause of 11:2 beside a WEB quotation that renders a different clause. The Hebrew quoted is the announcement (web:Dan.11.2 “Now I will show you the truth”); the English set beside it is the verse's second sentence, about three more kings. A reader takes the second as the rendering of the first.

suggested_fix.fact: the Hebrew opening clause of 11:2 is the announcement of the truth, and its rendering is the first sentence of the verse; the three kings belong to the next clause, which begins with a behold

W6-006.claim: In the onset sentence the Hebrew splice from 11:2 (וְעַתָּ֕ה אֱמֶ֖ת אַגִּ֣יד לָ֑ךְ) is followed by a WEB quotation of a different clause of 11:2 (the three kings); the WEB words that render the splice are the verse's first sentence, about showing the truth, so the English set beside the Hebrew is not its gloss.

suggested_fix.fact: the English paired with the 11:2 splice is the opening sentence of WEB 11:2 (now I will show you the truth), the pairing the neighbouring preamble row already uses

W6-007.claim: The unit stands as form: it opens on the succession wording of 11:7 and closes before the temporal marker of 11:14, and it says plainly that neither edge is strong. One provenance defect: the last sentence of device_notes says the year words at 11:8 and 11:13 are not datelines and carries no tier. suggested_fix.fact: the classing of the year words at 11:8 and 11:13 as not datelines is held by the device census, which lists both verses among year-word verses that are not datelines; the claim takes the tier of a fact read from that layer

W6-009.claim: The device notes of the row over 11:21-11:28 state that no ketiv/qere note and no paseq falls in the span, and that the 11:28/11:29 edge is one-sided, without any tier word and without naming the layer or its single witness. The unit itself holds: the succession formula opens 11:21 and the doubled return of 11:28 closes the first southern campaign.

suggested_fix.fact: The absence of ketiv/qere notes and paseq signs in 11:21-11:28 is a range claim read from the mark layer (WLC (OSHB), one witness) and owes its tier and layer; the weighing of the 11:28/11:29 edge is a reading and owes INFERRED.

W6-015.claim: One evidence ref of the row over 12:9-12:13 carries five consecutive WEB words of web:Dan.12.12 (the beatitude's opening) without quotation marks or a web reference. The unit itself is coherent as a single reply: it opens and closes on the charge to go (12:9 word 2, 12:13 word 2), the day counts of 12:11-12:12 and the beatitude stay inside it, and the book ends at 12:13. Its onset is the answer to the question of 12:8 and so shares the mark-led seam assessed under the row before it; the row says so plainly.

suggested_fix.fact: The gloss on the beatitude of 12:12 repeats five consecutive WEB words and owes either the quotation form with its web reference or a paraphrase.

W6-015.claim: The evidence tag on oshb:Dan.12.12 holds five consecutive WEB words ('blessed is he who waits', the opening of web:Dan.12.12, a verse inside the span) with no curly quotes and no web: reference in that field.
